Connecting the remote DataForSEO MCP server using OAuth – DataForSEO
excerpts:
1. 1 Claude Desktop connection
2. 2 ChatGPT connection
3. 3 Cursor connection
DataForSEO MCP server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol that allows popular LLMs and AI-powered tools to interact with our APIs and fetch data. In this guide, we’ll demonstrate how to connect to the DataForSEO MCP server remotely, using the OAuth protocol .
Using the remote MCP connection method, you don’t need to make any preparations on your device, such as creating configuration folders or running commands in Terminal or the Command Line. This method is completely no-code, and the OAuth protocol enables fast, secure authentication with your DataForSEO account.
This guide showcases connection workflows for the three most popular AI solutions: Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, and Cursor.
Contents:
Claude Desktop connection ChatGPT connection Cursor connection

1 Claude Desktop connection

Before setting everything up, make sure you have the following:
1. Claude Desktop installed on your device.
2. An active Claude account with Pro subscription.
3. An active DataForSEO account .
Here is the connection process step-by-step:
1. Open Claude Desktop and click on Customize in the upper left corner.
Claude 1
2. In the menu that appears, select Connectors . Then, click on the Plus (+) button and choose Add custom connector .
Claude 2
3. Give the connection a meaningful name, and in the URL field, paste the following DataForSEO MCP server URL:
mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp
Click Add .
Claude 3
4. On the Connector page, click Connect .
Claude 4
5. You will be redirected to the DataForSEO authentication flow page. Click Approve to establish the connection. After that, return to the Claude Desktop.
Claude 5
6. The connection is ready. Now, you can configure MCP tool permissions before using them in Claude.
Claude 6

2 ChatGPT connection

Before setting everything up, make sure you have the following:
1. An active ChatGPT account .
2. An active DataForSEO account .
The connection process is as follows:
1. In ChatGPT, open Settings → Plugins → Developer mode and enable the Developer mode . GPT 1
2. Go back to Plugins and click a + icon to create a new plugin.
GPT 2 3. In the menu that opens, write an app (connection) name of your choice, tick the box with the “I understand and want to continue” message, and paste the following DataForSEO MCP URL into the Connection field:
mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp
Select the OAuth authentication method and click Create .
GPT 3
4. Then, you will be asked to sign in with your connection and redirected to the DataForSEO authentication flow page. Click Approve to establish the connection. After that, return to the ChatGPT.
GPT 4
5. The connection is ready. Now, you can try DataForSEO MCP tools in a conversation with ChatGPT.
GPT 5

3 Cursor connection

Before setting everything up, make sure you have the following:
1. Cursor app installed on your device.
2. An active DataForSEO account .
Here is the connection process step-by-step:
1. Open Cursor and click on the Settings button in the upper right corner.
Cursor 1
2. Navigate to Tools & MCPs and click Add Custom MCP .
Cursor 2
3. In the window that opens, paste the following JSON configuration snippet:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dataforseo": {
      "url": "mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp"
    }
  }
}
Save and close.
Cursor 3
4. The Cursor will ask for authentication. Click Connect .
Cursor 4
5. You will be redirected to the DataForSEO authentication flow page. Click Approve to establish the connection. After that, return to Cursor.
Cursor 5
6. The connection is ready. Now, you can use DataForSEO MCP tools in your Cursor projects and agents.
Cursor 6

excerpts:
### DataForSEO API key: FAQ

#### How do I get my DataForSEO API key?

Create a free account, log in, and open the **API Access** tab in the dashboard sidebar. Our system generates your API login and API password, and the two, encoded in Base64, are your API key. On older accounts, the login may still be your sign-up email. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

#### Where do I find my API password?

It’s in the **API Access** tab of your dashboard. Don’t confuse it with your account password: that one logs you into the dashboard, and only the API password works for API requests. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

...

#### How do I encode my DataForSEO credentials with Base64?

Join your login and API password with a colon ( `login:password` ) and encode that string with Base64. You can copy a ready-made encoded string from the **API Access** tab in the first 24 hours and request it by email after that, or make one yourself with a trusted online encoder or a one-line terminal command. Make and n8n do the encoding for you, so you can skip this step there. Jump to Step 2: encode your credentials with Base64

Here’s the full setup.

### Step 1 — Get your API credentials from the dashboard

Create a free account on our website. New accounts get a $1 trial credit, and the SERP Google Organic Live Advanced endpoint costs $0.002 per call, so the trial covers around 500 live Google SERPs before you spend a cent. Enough room to set things up and run a few tests.

...

#### Make.com

In your Make scenario, add an HTTP module and set the method to POST. Under **Credentials** , create a new **Basic Auth** connection. Paste your DataForSEO API login into **Username** and your API password into **Password** . Make handles Base64 encoding for you and adds the right `Authorization` header to every request. Save the connection and reuse it across scenarios.

#### n8n

Add an **HTTP Request** node to your workflow. Set the method to POST and paste the DataForSEO endpoint URL. Under **Authentication** , select **Generic Credential Type** , then choose **Basic Auth** in the **Generic Auth Type** dropdown. Enter your API login as the username and your API password as the password. n8n encodes Base64 for you. For a no-code workflow built on this pattern, see our walkthrough on [automating keyword research with n8n and DataForSEO](dataforseo.com/help-center/automate-keyword-research-with-n8n-and-dataforseo) .

excerpts:
Once you [log in to your DataForSEO Dashboard](app.dataforseo.com/signin) , you can open this section from the left-hand navigation menu or by using the shortcut in the top bar. Clicking either option will open the [API Access](app.dataforseo.com/api-access) section where your API credentials are.

The API credentials include:

* **API login** — a unique, automatically generated string used to identify your account when making API requests.
* **API password** — a secure password automatically generated by DataForSEO for API authentication.

You can use these credentials to connect DataForSEO APIs to tools like Postman, Make, n8n, Google Sheets connectors, or your own applications.

[dataforseo dashboard api access](dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/dataforseo-dashboard-api-access.webp)

**Changing your API login**

If you need to update your API login, you can do so in the API Access section of your Dashboard.

[change api login dataforseo](dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/change-api-login-dataforseo.png)

Keep in mind that your API login is used to authenticate API requests. After changing it, make sure to update the credentials in any applications, integrations, or workflows connected to DataForSEO.

**API password visibility and recovery**

Your API login always remains visible in the Dashboard. Your API password is visible only during the first 24 hours after registration. After that, it is hidden for security reasons. If you need your API password later, click _Send by e-mail_ , and the password will be sent to the email address you used to create your DataForSEO account.

**Base64-encoded API credentials**

For the first 24 hours after registration, the API Access tab displays a ready-made, Base64-encoded string of your `login:password` . It disappears later for the same security reason your API password does, but you can similarly request it by email at any time.

excerpts:
6. FAQ & troubleshooting

The [DataForSEO MCP server](dataforseo.com/model-context-protocol) is a powerful tool that allows the seamless integration of DataForSEO [APIs](dataforseo.com/apis) and enables advanced SEO data analytics capabilities. This simple guide will walk you through the process of setting up and using the official [DataForSEO MCP server](github.com/dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript) .

### What is DataForSEO MCP server?

DataForSEO MCP server is the implementation of the [Model Context Protocol](modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) , allowing AI tools to obtain and process data from DataForSEO. In a nutshell, this MCP server is a bridge between AI models and our APIs, so that you can easily extract data and turn it into insights without writing a single line of code.

**This article will cover the following:**

Quick start: connect from your AI tool or client  
Run without installation  
Advanced setup: run from source  
Streamable HTTP  
FAQ & troubleshooting

...

### Run without installation

The easiest way to run the DataForSEO MCP server is with `npx` . This way you always get the latest published version without needing a local installation.

Before getting started, make sure:

* You installed the latest version of [Node.js](nodejs.org/en/download) .
* You have a DataForSEO account with your [API login and password](app.dataforseo.com/api-access) .

1 Set your environment variables. Remember to replace `your_username` and `your_password` with your actual DataForSEO [API login and password.](app.dataforseo.com/api-access)

...

2 Run with `npx` to start the server using the `stdio` (standard input/output) protocol.

```
npx dataforseo-mcp-server
```

You can choose between different protocols depending on your client’s compatibility.

➤ **HTTP server.** Most modern MCP-compatible clients (except Claude Desktop) expect this protocol.

```
npx dataforseo-mcp-server http
```

...

Use this URL (no local setup).

```
mcp.dataforseo.com/mcp
```

### Advanced setup: run from source

If you prefer to run the server from source for development or offline use, follow the instructions in our [GitHub repository.](github.com/dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript) You can also [check this video for details.](youtube.com/embed/4C6dgxiQIpY)

### FAQ & troubleshooting

#### Auth errors (“you are not authorized…”)

This is the most common issue. Solutions:

* Make sure you’re using your [API credentials (login and password)](app.dataforseo.com/api-access) for making API calls, not your account login and password for logging into DataForSEO Dashboard.
* Note that the required format of API credentials depends on the client. Some tools only need you to enter your API login and API password into separate lines in the interface. ChatGPT with remote server requires an authorization header with `your_api_login:your_api_password` encoded in the Base64 format like in this example:
```
Basic ZGVtb19sb2dpbjpkZW1vX3Bhc3N3b3Jk
```

# Introduction

### Welcome to DataForSEO API!

This is the starting point on your journey towards building powerful SEO software, data analysis pipelines, and robust no-code automations. With DataForSEO you can get all the data you need while saving your time and budget.

### Getting started

Follow our recommended learning path to master DataForSEO APIs.

1. Kickstart Guide to our APIs  
2. Dashboard Guide  
3. Test with API Playground  
4. Free Unlimited Trial Info  
5. Sandbox Best Practices

### REST technology

DataForSEO API is using the REST technology for interchanging data between your application and our service. The data exchange is made through the widely used HTTP protocol, which allows applying our API to almost all programming languages.

### Client libraries

You can create your REST class or use the following ready-made classes:

### PHP, Python, C# and Postman examples

Choose your preferred programming language or API testing tool.

### Data encoding

All data you send to DataForSEO API should be UTF-8 encoded.

If you use one of the Clients listed in the first table, gzip will be the default format of data exchange. You will see

```
Content-Encoding: gzip
```

in the header.

All the responses are returned in the JSON format by default, but we also support responses in the XML format – just append

```
.xml
```

to the end of your request. In addition to that, you can request HTML results from endpoints that return HTML-encoded results by appending

```
.html
```

to the end of the request’s URL path.

For example, the following requests will return response encoded in XML or HTML accordingly:  
https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/user\_data.xml
  
https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task\_get/html/09061543-1535-0066-0000-6240830f56ba.html

### Rate limits

Each of DataForSEO APIs has a certain rate limit, which you can find in the HTTP header of every endpoint.

Rate limit HTTP headers we use:  

```
X-RateLimit-Limit
```

– the rate limit ceiling per minute for the given endpoint;  

```
X-RateLimit-Remaining
```

– the number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window.

If your system requires rate limits to be increased, please contact our support team.

### Results storage

The term for storing API results in our system depends on the API and method of data retrieval.

* Standard method: results are stored for 30 days\*
* Live method: results are not stored\*
* HTML results: results are stored for 7 days

\*for SERP API in both Standard and Live methods, the results in JSON format are stored for 30 days.

To learn more about the terms of results storage, check this Help Center article.

# How to Authenticate with DataForSEO Google Search SERP API: API Key Setup and Code Examples

SERP API

Updated 18.11.2026

Table of Contents

Your DataForSEO API key is your API login and API password, joined as `login:password` and encoded in Base64. You’ll find both in the **API Access** tab of your dashboard, and the steps below show how to use them in Make, n8n, Custom GPTs, and cURL.

The setup is simpler than the words around it suggest, even if API key, token, Basic Auth, and Base64 sound intimidating when you’re not a developer. Authentication is one of the easier parts of working with our APIs. You set up one credential pair, encode it once, and use it in whichever tool you’ve already got open: Make, n8n, Custom GPTs, scripts, AI agents.

If you’re here for a Google Search API key example, you’re in the right place. This guide walks you through finding your credentials, encoding them, and getting them into that tool.

### Setting up Google Search API authentication: what you need to know

When you’re searching for “Google Search API,” you’re probably looking for DataForSEO Google Organic SERP API. It’s a live source of Google search results, including featured snippets, AI Overviews, and other SERP features. We’ll use it as the example throughout this article, though DataForSEO authentication works the same across all our APIs. Set it up once, and you’re done.

A quick glossary first, so the rest of the post reads cleanly.

* **API login.** A unique string our system generates to identify your account in API requests. On older accounts, the sign-up email may still function as the API login, however the owner can change it and switch to a generated one.
* **API password.** A separate password is automatically generated when you register an account with DataForSEO. It’s not the same as the password you use to log into the dashboard. This one authenticates your API requests.
* **Basic Auth.** Short for Basic Authentication. Instead of a single API key string, you send your API login and password with every request. It’s the simplest authentication pattern on the web, which is why we picked it.
* **Base64.** A format for safely passing characters like `:` and `@` through HTTP headers. Base64 is encoding, not encryption — anyone with the encoded string can decode it, so treat it like a password.
* **Header.** The part of an HTTP request that carries metadata, including your credentials. Your encoded API login and password go in an `Authorization` header of every call.

That’s the vocabulary out of the way. If you came here with one specific question, check the short answers below before the full setup.

### DataForSEO API key: FAQ

#### How do I get my DataForSEO API key?

Create a free account, log in, and open the **API Access** tab in the dashboard sidebar. Our system generates your API login and API password, and the two, encoded in Base64, are your API key. On older accounts, the login may still be your sign-up email. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

#### Where do I find my API password?

It’s in the **API Access** tab of your dashboard. Don’t confuse it with your account password: that one logs you into the dashboard, and only the API password works for API requests. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

#### Why can’t I see my API password in the dashboard?

The dashboard shows your API password for the first 24 hours after registration, then hides it for security reasons. After that, click **Send by e-mail** and we’ll resend it to the address on your account. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

#### Is the DataForSEO API key the same as my login password?

No. Your login password only gets you into the dashboard. The API key is built from a separate API password that our system generates for you, and mixing the two up is one of the usual reasons a request fails. Jump to Common authentication mistakes

# Connecting the remote DataForSEO MCP server using OAuth

DataForSEO MCP

Updated 07.08.2026

Table of Contents

DataForSEO MCP server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol that allows popular LLMs and AI-powered tools to interact with our APIs and fetch data. In this guide, we’ll demonstrate how to connect to the DataForSEO MCP server remotely, using the OAuth protocol.

Using the remote MCP connection method, you don’t need to make any preparations on your device, such as creating configuration folders or running commands in Terminal or the Command Line. This method is completely no-code, and the OAuth protocol enables fast, secure authentication with your DataForSEO account.

This guide showcases connection workflows for the three most popular AI solutions: Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, and Cursor.

**Contents:**

### 1 Claude Desktop connection

Before setting everything up, make sure you have the following:

1. Claude Desktop installed on your device.
2. An active Claude account with Pro subscription.
3. An active DataForSEO account.

Here is the connection process step-by-step:

**1.** Open Claude Desktop and click on **Customize** in the upper left corner.

**2.** In the menu that appears, select **Connectors**. Then, click on the **Plus (+)** button and choose **Add custom connector**.

**3.** Give the connection a meaningful name, and in the **URL** field, paste the following DataForSEO MCP server URL:

`https://mcp.dataforseo.com/mcp`

Click **Add**.

**4.** On the Connector page, click **Connect**.

**5.** You will be redirected to the DataForSEO authentication flow page. Click **Approve** to establish the connection. After that, return to the Claude Desktop.

**6.** The connection is ready. Now, you can configure MCP tool permissions before using them in Claude.

### 2 ChatGPT connection

Before setting everything up, make sure you have the following:

1. An active ChatGPT account.
2. An active DataForSEO account.

The connection process is as follows:

**1.** In ChatGPT, open **Settings → Plugins → Developer mode** and enable the **Developer mode**.

**2.** Go back to **Plugins** and click a **+** icon to create a new plugin.

**3.** In the menu that opens, write an app (connection) name of your choice, tick the box with the *“I understand and want to continue”* message, and paste the following DataForSEO MCP URL into the **Connection** field:

`https://mcp.dataforseo.com/mcp`

Select the **OAuth** authentication method and click **Create**.

**4.** Then, you will be asked to sign in with your connection and redirected to the DataForSEO authentication flow page. Click **Approve** to establish the connection. After that, return to the ChatGPT.

**5.** The connection is ready. Now, you can try DataForSEO MCP tools in a conversation with ChatGPT.

### 3 Cursor connection

Before setting everything up, make sure you have the following:

1. Cursor app installed on your device.
2. An active DataForSEO account.

Here is the connection process step-by-step:

**1.** Open **Cursor** and click on the **Settings** button in the upper right corner.

**2.** Navigate to **Tools & MCPs** and click **Add Custom MCP**.

**3.** In the window that opens, paste the following JSON configuration snippet:

```

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dataforseo": {
      "url": "https://mcp.dataforseo.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Save and close.

**4.** The Cursor will ask for authentication. Click **Connect**.

**5.** You will be redirected to the DataForSEO authentication flow page. Click **Approve** to establish the connection. After that, return to Cursor.

**6.** The connection is ready. Now, you can use DataForSEO MCP tools in your Cursor projects and agents.
